title: “Venerable sir, thus a person has no stain but does not truly know: ‘There is no stain in me.’ For such a person, it can…
content: “Venerable sir, thus a person has no stain but does not truly know: ‘There is no stain in me.’ For such a person, it can be expected: ‘He will attend to the sign of the beautiful. By attending to the sign of the beautiful, greed will pollute his mind. He will die with greed, with ill-will, with delusion, with stain, his mind polluted.’”

title: Hemavata: “Is he without desire for sensual pleasures? Is his mind undisturbed? Has he overcome all delusion? Does he truly have eyes for all things?”…
content:
Hemavata:
“Is he without desire for sensual pleasures?
Is his mind undisturbed?
Has he overcome all delusion?
Does he truly have eyes for all things?”

Sātāgira:
“He has no desire for sensual pleasures,
His mind is undisturbed,
He has overcome all delusion —
The Buddha truly has eyes for all things.”

title: - What closes in the world? Upon what does the world stand? What hangs up the world? What envelops the world? - Death closes in…
content:
- What closes in the world?
Upon what does the world stand?
What hangs up the world?
What envelops the world?
- Death closes in the world,
Upon suffering the world stands,
Craving hangs up the world,
Aging envelops the world.

title: “And how, good sirs, is one defiled by sensual lust? Here, good sirs, when a monk sees a form with the eye, he is attached…
content: “And how, good sirs, is one defiled by sensual lust? Here, good sirs, when a monk sees a form with the eye, he is attached to agreeable forms and repelled by disagreeable forms. He dwells with bodily mindfulness unestablished, with a limited mind. He does not know as it actually is the liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom. Here, evil, unwholesome states that have arisen are not abandoned without remainder. When he tastes a flavor with the tongue … When he cognizes a phenomenon with the mind, he is attached to agreeable phenomena and repelled by disagreeable phenomena. He dwells with bodily mindfulness unestablished, with a limited mind. He does not know as it actually is the liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom. Here, evil, unwholesome states that have arisen are not abandoned without remainder. This, good sirs, is called a monk who is defiled by sensual lust regarding forms cognizable by the eye … regarding tastes … regarding phenomena cognizable by the mind. A monk living thus, good sirs, if Māra approaches him through the eye, Māra gains an opportunity, Māra gains an object. If Māra approaches him through the tongue … through the mind, Māra gains an opportunity, Māra gains an object.”

title: “One who once was heedless and later is not, Illumines the world like the moon freed from clouds.” “He who deeds of merit makes, And…
content:
“One who once was heedless and later is not,
Illumines the world like the moon freed from clouds.”

“He who deeds of merit makes,
And thereby his evil deeds dispels,
Illumines the world like the moon freed from clouds.”

“Blinded is this world,
Few are those who see clearly.
Like birds escaped from a net,
Few go to heaven.”

“Like a swan flying through the sky,
With psychic power soaring through space,
Having conquered Māra and his host,
The wise one leaves this world behind.”

title: “He contemplates all forms, feelings, perceptions, formations, and consciousness as impermanent, as suffering, as a disease, as a boil, as a dart, as misery, as…
content: “He contemplates all forms, feelings, perceptions, formations, and consciousness as impermanent, as suffering, as a disease, as a boil, as a dart, as misery, as an affliction, as alien, as disintegrating, as empty, as not-self. He turns his mind away from these states and directs it towards the deathless element: ‘This is peaceful, this is sublime—namely, the stilling of all formations, the relinquishment of all attachments, the destruction of craving, dispassion, cessation, Nibbāna.’ If he is firm in this, he attains the destruction of the defilements. If he does not yet attain the destruction of the defilements, then by that same Dhamma-lust, Dhamma-delight, and by the destruction of the five lower fetters, he becomes one who is reborn spontaneously (in the Pure Abodes) and there attains final Nibbāna, never to return from that world.”

title: “And Nigrodha, there are unwholesome states that have not been abandoned, that are defiling, leading to renewed existence, bringing suffering, resulting in pain, leading to…
content: “And Nigrodha, there are unwholesome states that have not been abandoned, that are defiling, leading to renewed existence, bringing suffering, resulting in pain, leading to future birth, aging, and death. Those states I teach for the purpose of abandoning them. If you practice in accordance with the teaching, then those defiling states will be abandoned, the pure states will increase, and you will personally know, realize, and attain to abiding here and now with perfect and complete wisdom.”

title: “O good friends, here someone associates with sensual pleasures, associates with unwholesome states. After some time, that person hears the noble Dhamma, gives wise attention,…
content: “O good friends, here someone associates with sensual pleasures, associates with unwholesome states. After some time, that person hears the noble Dhamma, gives wise attention, and attains the true Dhamma and the Dhamma in accordance. And having heard the noble Dhamma, given wise attention, and attained the true Dhamma and the Dhamma in accordance, that person lives without associating with sensual pleasures, without associating with unwholesome states. By living without associating with sensual pleasures, without associating with unwholesome states, ease arises, and more than ease, gladness arises. O good friends, just as from comfort joy is born, so too, O good friends, by living without associating with sensual pleasures, without associating with unwholesome states, ease arises, and more than ease, gladness arises. O good friends, that is the first short path leading to ease, realized by the Blessed One, the Wise One, the Seer, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One.

title: “Monks, how does a monk live as an island unto himself, a refuge unto himself, seeking no other refuge; with the Dhamma as his island,…
content: “Monks, how does a monk live as an island unto himself, a refuge unto himself, seeking no other refuge; with the Dhamma as his island, with the Dhamma as his refuge, seeking no other refuge? Monks, here a monk abides contemplating the body as a body internally, ardent, diligent, mindful, clearly comprehending, to remove covetousness and sorrow in the world; abides contemplating feelings as feelings … mind as mind … phenomena as phenomena, ardent, diligent, mindful, clearly comprehending, to remove covetousness and sorrow in the world. Thus, monks, a monk lives as an island unto himself, a refuge unto himself, seeking no other refuge; with the Dhamma as his island, with the Dhamma as his refuge, seeking no other refuge.”

title: “Cunda, just as all unwholesome states tend downward and all wholesome states tend upward. So too, Cunda: the harmless person is higher than the harmful…
content: “Cunda, just as all unwholesome states tend downward and all wholesome states tend upward. So too, Cunda: the harmless person is higher than the harmful person; the person who abstains from killing is higher than the killer; the person who abstains from taking what is not given is higher than the taker of what is not given; the person unsmeared by the world, not clinging to personal views, of easy disposition and equanimity, is higher than the person smeared by the world, clinging to personal views, of difficult disposition and lacking equanimity.”
